claim.why_it_matters: Same page-boundary defect: 'Miao:' from the top of page 987 is merged onto the Meroitic_Hieroglyphs range line, orphaning the Miao ranges.

verdict.reasoning: Both sides were checked directly and the claim quotes each accurately. RENDERED PDF (spec_p1016.png, 300dpi, printed page 986): the page is single-column, left-aligned, and its final two content lines are 'Meroitic_Hieroglyphs:' / '10980-1099F'. A dedicated crop of the bottom 20% of the page shows clean whitespace from there down to the footer '986 (C)ISO/IEC 2023' and the licence line - there is no 'Miao:' anywhere on page 986, in the right margin or otherwise. RENDERED PDF page 1017 (printed 987) begins its body with 'Miao:' / '16F00-16F4A, 16F50, 16F93-16F9F', exactly as the claim states. MARKDOWN (specs/ISO_COBOL.md, verified byte-exact with cat -A at lines 40505-40512): line 40506 reads '10980-1099F Miao:' and the first content line after the page-1017 furniture is the bare range list '16F00-16F4A, 16F50, 16F93-16F9F'. I considered and rejected the standard refutations. (a) Not lost text: 'Miao:' is present and still precedes its ranges in reading order. (b) Not page-break furniture: the furniture here is the anchor, the '## Page 1017' marker, the running header and the page number; 'Miao:' is spec content, and it has been emitted on the WRONG PAGE, which is precisely the fidelity property this reconciliation checks. (c) Not mere line wrapping: this list is a two-line-per-entry structure in which the line boundary IS the name-to-ranges binding, so moving the label onto the preceding entry's data line changes what the text asserts - page 1016 now ends with a malformed entry whose range list carries a spurious trailing token, and page 1017 opens with a range list that has no owning script name. (d) Not curable by cross-reference: the second copy of this script list later in the file (lines 49306-49310) is a different table with different Miao ranges (16F00-16F4A, 16F4F-16F87, 16F8F-16F9F), so it cannot stand in for this one. Corroborating evidence that this is a systematic page-split off-by-one rather than an isolated reflow: the identical defect sits at the 1015/1016 boundary, where line 40454 reads '10600-10736, 10740-10755, 10760-10767 Linear_B:' - and as a direct consequence page 1016's own markdown body starts at the bare ranges '10000-1000B, ...' with its 'Linear_B:' label missing, even though the PDF plainly prints 'Linear_B:' as the first line of page 986. Page 1016 is therefore damaged by this defect in both directions: it has lost its own opening label and gained the next page's opening label.
verdict.corrected_description: CONFIRMED, with two refinements. (1) Nothing is deleted - 'Miao:' survives and still precedes its ranges in linear reading order; the defect is placement, not omission. The concrete damage is structural: the Meroitic_Hieroglyphs entry ends '10980-1099F Miao:' with a spurious trailing token, and the first content line of page 1017 is an unlabelled range list, so any line-structured read of the script-name-to-code-point-ranges table mis-binds both entries. (2) The claim understates the blast radius on this page. The same page-split off-by-one also pulled 'Linear_B:' off the top of page 986 onto the tail of page 1015 (line 40454: '10600-10736, 10740-10755, 10760-10767 Linear_B:'), so the markdown for page 1016 additionally OPENS with an orphaned range list '10000-1000B, 1000D-10026, ...' whose 'Linear_B:' label is absent, though the PDF prints it as page 986's first line. Page 1016 is thus mis-split at both boundaries: one label lost to the previous page, one label stolen from the next.
